2609.18720.title: LocQE: Principled Domain Adaptation for Localisation Quality Estimation by Leveraging Post-Edits
2609.18720.paper_summary: Learned quality estimation (QE) models such as COMETKiwi are widespread and work well for general machine translation evaluation. However, they are known to struggle on unseen domains, limiting their performance in a real-world localisation context. We show that they are insensitive to some important factors in localisation, such as whether numbers are translated accurately, or even whether the correct number of spaces and punctuation are preserved in a translation. Further, a key capability for optimisation of machine translation is the ability of QE models to accurately rank different translations of a single segment, which suffers significantly from the domain transfer. In the absence of large-scale direct assessment data, we propose principled fine-tuning approaches to reduce the domain gap with even small amounts of post-editing data. Using a multi-task fine-tuning approach and a simple tokeniser intervention, we create a QE model which proves markedly better at distinguishing preferred post-edits from rejected initial translations in a localisation context. We show that preferences and artificial continuous scores stabilise each other, and argue that to calibrate metrics both in terms of their absolute scores and comparisons between translation of the same source, both types of signal are needed.
2609.18720.paper_summary_zh: 學習的質量估計（QE）模型，如 COMETKiwi，廣泛應用並且在一般機器翻譯評估中表現良好。<lb/>然而，它們在未見過的領域中表現不佳，限制了它們在現實世界本地化環境中的性能。<lb/>我們顯示它們對於本地化中的一些重要因素不敏感，例如數字是否被準確翻譯，甚至翻譯中是否保留了正確的空格和標點符號數量。<lb/>此外，機器翻譯優化的一個關鍵能力是 QE 模型準確排名單一段落的不同翻譯，而這在領域轉移中受到顯著影響。<lb/>在缺乏大規模直接評估數據的情況下，我們提出了原則性的微調方法，以減少領域差距，即使在少量後編輯數據的情況下也是如此。<lb/>通過多任務微調方法和簡單的分詞干預，我們創建了一個 QE 模型，該模型在本地化環境中明顯更擅長區分首選的後編輯和被拒絕的初始翻譯。<lb/>我們顯示偏好和人工連續分數彼此穩定，並主張為了校準指標，無論是在其絕對分數還是同一來源翻譯之間的比較方面，都需要這兩種類型的信號。
